title: Retrieval-augmented generation and grounded answers
text: Retrieval-augmented generation searches an external corpus for passages and supplies them as context before a language model generates its answer.

title: Citation support and faithfulness in RAG
text: Context retrieval, citation support, source attribution, and answer faithfulness distinguish grounded RAG from an unsupported answer produced only from model parameters.

title: Prompt injection against an AI agent
text: A prompt injection is an untrusted instruction that attempts to redirect a model or agent away from its governing policy, sometimes through retrieved content.

title: Indirect injection and instruction hierarchy
text: Phrases such as ignore previous instructions, an indirect injection in a document, instruction-hierarchy conflict, and attempted tool exfiltration diagnose prompt injection.

title: Hallucination in a generative model
text: A model hallucination is a fluent but unsupported or factually wrong claim. The response may sound plausible even though no available evidence supports it.

title: Plausible-but-false model claims
text: Missing evidence, fabricated citations, internal inconsistency, and plausible-but-false factual content are hallucination indicators rather than retrieval or ranking failures alone.

title: Concept drift after model deployment
text: Concept drift occurs when the relationship between production inputs and prediction targets changes over time, causing a once-valid model to become stale.

title: Rolling performance under a regime shift
text: A post-deployment shift, seasonal regime, sustained decline in rolling performance, and a drift-detector alarm distinguish concept drift from a one-off bad example.

title: Training-data poisoning and backdoors
text: Training-data poisoning corrupts examples before or during learning so that the resulting model changes behavior or responds to an attacker-chosen backdoor trigger.

title: Trigger patterns and label flipping
text: A trigger pattern, label flipping, compromised training pipeline, and preserved clean accuracy with targeted failure are diagnostic of data poisoning.

title: Adversarial examples at inference time
text: An adversarial example is a deliberately perturbed test input that makes an otherwise unchanged classifier predict the wrong class.

title: Epsilon-bounded gradient attack
text: An imperceptible epsilon-bounded perturbation, gradient-based optimization, unchanged model weights, and reduced robust accuracy identify a test-time adversarial attack.

title: Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning
text: Catastrophic forgetting happens when sequential training on a new task overwrites representations needed for earlier tasks and old-task performance collapses.

title: Replay and retention across a task sequence
text: A task sequence, falling retention score, recovery with a replay buffer, or elastic weight consolidation distinguish catastrophic forgetting.

title: Second-stage retrieval reranking
text: Retrieval reranking applies a richer relevance model to an initial candidate set and reorders documents before they reach the answer generator.

title: Cross-encoder top-k reranker
text: A cross-encoder scores query-document pairs in the top k, improves MRR through pairwise relevance, and operates after first-stage retrieval.

title: Low-precision model quantization
text: Quantization stores weights or activations at lower precision to reduce model memory, inference latency, energy use, and hardware cost.

title: INT8 and four-bit calibration
text: INT8 or four-bit weights, a representative calibration set, integer inference, and measured quantization error distinguish quantization from pruning or distillation.

title: Sparse mixture-of-experts model
text: A mixture-of-experts network uses a learned router to send each token or example to a small subset of specialized neural expert blocks.

title: Top-k routing and expert load balance
text: Sparse activation, top-k experts, capacity limits, and an auxiliary load-balancing loss diagnose mixture-of-experts routing.

title: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
text: RLHF collects human preference comparisons, learns a reward model, and optimizes a language-model policy toward responses people prefer.

title: Preference pairs, policy optimization, and reward hacking
text: Preference pairs, human ranking, policy optimization against a reward model, and the risk of reward hacking distinguish RLHF from supervised fine-tuning alone.

title: Tool-calling AI agent loop
text: A tool-calling agent emits a structured action, invokes an external function or API, observes the result, and continues its reasoning loop.

title: Function schema and execution boundary
text: A function schema, explicit tool result, action-observation loop, and a validated execution boundary distinguish tool use from free-text generation.

title: Coordination in a multi-agent system
text: A multi-agent system assigns specialized roles, delegates subtasks, and exchanges messages so several agents can pursue a shared objective.

title: Message protocol and shared state for agent teams
text: Role specialization, a message protocol, shared state, dependency management, and detectable coordination failure distinguish multi-agent coordination.

title: Embedding drift in vector retrieval
text: Embedding drift occurs when an encoder update or changing input population moves vectors and alters the similarity relationships used for retrieval.

title: Centroid shift and nearest-neighbor instability
text: A centroid shift, nearest-neighbor instability across encoder versions, and degrading retrieval relevance are direct embedding-drift diagnostics.

title: Differential privacy guarantee
text: Differential privacy uses randomized mechanisms so the presence or absence of one individual's record has a bounded effect on released results.

title: Epsilon-delta privacy accounting
text: Neighboring datasets, calibrated noise, epsilon and delta, composition, and a tracked privacy budget identify a differential-privacy mechanism.

title: Federated learning across clients
text: Federated learning sends a model to clients for local training and aggregates their updates while raw client data remains decentralized.

title: Federated averaging with non-IID clients
text: Client communication rounds, secure aggregation, non-IID local datasets, and federated averaging distinguish federated learning from ordinary centralized training.

title: Teacher-student knowledge distillation
text: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student to imitate probabilities, logits, or internal representations produced by a larger teacher model.

title: Soft targets and distillation temperature
text: Teacher predictions, temperature-scaled logits, a distillation loss, and student compression distinguish knowledge distillation from direct low-precision quantization.

title: Evaluation protocol for a language model
text: LLM evaluation defines tasks, test data, metrics, rubrics, and reporting rules to measure model quality, safety, calibration, robustness, cost, and latency.

title: Confidence and contamination controls in LLM evaluation
text: A human rubric or validated LLM-as-judge, confidence intervals, paired comparisons, and test-contamination controls characterize a rigorous LLM evaluation.

title: Finite context window in a language model
text: A context window is the finite number of tokens a model can process in one request. Longer prompts require truncation, selection, or compression.

title: Token budget and lost-in-the-middle behavior
text: A hard token budget, context truncation, long-context degradation, and lost-in-the-middle behavior distinguish a context-window limitation.

title: Cost-aware routing across language models
text: An LLM router chooses among model tiers for each task to balance expected answer quality, monetary price, latency, availability, and capacity.

title: Per-task cost, fallback, and quality gates
text: Per-task cost, a quality threshold, latency budget, fallback model, and routing policy distinguish cost-aware LLM routing from model compression.
